biur-halacha/1:א: (א) And through eiruv, etc. — see Mishna Berurah: the prohibition is only d'rabbanan because of the reasoning of ho'il, since guests may arrive; therefore eiruv helps — so wrote Magen Avraham in the name of Ran, like Rabbah in Pesachim 47 and Milchamot in Beitzah [Magen Avraham wrote in the name of Maor and Chakham Tzvi challenged — the Maor wrote so only per Rif, but Milchamot holds so]. So too Tosafot Eruvin 48 first answer: for this reason baking and cooking are permitted and we are not concerned for hachanah d'oraisa; where ho'il does not apply, e.g. close to dark, Tosafot Pesachim 46 wrote it is d'oraisa — cited also in Rashba's chiddushim in Beitzah; Magen Avraham brought Mordechai: close to dark is forbidden, ho'il does not apply, eiruv does not help — so Hagahot Maimoniyot and Semag: all his French teachers hold Shabbat melachot are not done on Yom Tov except through ho'il; where ho'il does not apply it is d'oraisa. For these poskim melacha prohibition and hachanah are one, as Milchamot explains. However Ritzba in Eruvin 48 [Tosafot at the start of Beitzah in Stam is only Ritzba's view; Semag cited this only as a lone view] holds hachanah applies only to a new matter, not baking/cooking which is mere repair; therefore eiruv helps [if for melacha, his view is like Rav Chisda that Shabbat melachot are done on Yom Tov — see Ittur]. Meiri also distinguishes hachanah from melacha; melacha was permitted only due to ho'il per Tosafot, Semag, Ramban; for them close to dark is forbidden — Magen Avraham, Chemed Moshe, Gra wrote we therefore pray Maariv early when Yom Tov falls on erev Shabbat; Ateret Zekenim in Levush. However Rabbenu Efraim and Maor rule fully like Rav Chisda: Shabbat melachot on Yom Tov are d'oraisa with no distinction between earlier and close to dark. Rambam: although he rules like Rabbah that one who does melacha from Yom Tov to weekday is not lashed for ho'il, for Shabbat he adopts Rav Chisda that d'oraisa Shabbat melachot are done on Yom Tov, only d'rabbanan lest they be lenient also from Yom Tov to weekday [it appears even Yom Tov to weekday, though not lashed, is still d'oraisa — see his wording in halachah 9 and 13 ch. 1; Chemed Moshe elaborated]. Hagahot and Semag understood Rambam so; Beit Yosef on Rambam; plain wording; Chemed Moshe disagrees with Magen Avraham's diversion; Beit Meir concludes Rambam follows Rav Chisda: Shabbat needs are done on Yom Tov d'oraisa, unlike Maharshal and Magen Avraham — because Rav Ashi's plain words imply: lest they say from Yom Tov to Shabbat is forbidden, kal vachomer to weekday — thus d'oraisa permitted for Shabbat, per Rav Chisda, not ho'il [similarly Yerushalmi Yom Tov: by Torah it is forbidden and eiruv tavshilin permits; R' Avahu: by right one should bake/cook Yom Tov to Shabbat — if you say so, also Yom Tov to weekday]. Although Ramban reconciled Rav Ashi also to Rabbah — Milchamot — plain words follow Rav Chisda as Maor wrote; Pirush Chadash on Rav Chisda in Pesachim matches Rav Ashi in Beitzah — one view; this is Rambam's view; Ritzba in Tosafot Eruvin and Beitzah requires halacha like Rav Chisda [Chemed Moshe and Beit Meir: still melacha prohibition — see their discussion]. Thus l'chatchila one must be strict per these authorities on a d'oraisa matter as Acharonim wrote; b'dieved in pressing need one may rely on them for close to dark; Rosh and Tur did not cite Tosafot on close to dark [see Perishah]; Stam of Talmud permits with eiruv without distinction — all the more on second day of Yom Tov which is d'rabbanan one may rely leniently in need.

Hence one might say: only when he made eiruv but did not mention lighting it is permitted, but without any eiruv all forbid — yet Talmud explicitly: without any eiruv it is still permitted, as Beit Yosef and Shulchan Aruch imply; Avodat HaKodesh 45 implies the same for carrying; Hagahot Ashiri Beitzah ch. 2 eiruv formula for private domain to private domain — we do not say so; thus permitted, for candle lighting depends on this; Rama: even for those who say one does not mention lighting, nevertheless forbidden without eiruv tavshilin (nevertheless forbidden without eiruv); poskim above imply they are linked.

On this Mishnat Hasidim wrote siman 259: when Yom Tov is erev Shabbat it is fit to advance and insulate from erev Yom Tov the pot so it cook at least half-cooked from erev Yom Tov, see there. However some say Shabbat needs are done on Yom Tov from Torah as in Sefer Beit Meir and Chayei Adam letter 1 and Mishna Berurah in Biur Halacha; therefore wrote there in Mishna Berurah letter 3: in pressing need one may be lenient on second Yom Tov falling erev Shabbat if cooking for Shabbat was delayed until near Shabbat; and even on first Yom Tov perhaps leniency in pressing need — only l'chatchila certainly must beware, especially first Yom Tov which is d'oraisa, see there:

kaf-hachayyim/7:_: (ז) There. Through eiruv he cooks first for Shabbat. They relied on the verse Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it — remember it when it might be forgotten. Why? Rava: to prepare a good portion for Shabbat and Yom Tov. Rav Ashi: lest they say one does not bake from Yom Tov to Shabbat — kal vachomer from Yom Tov to weekday. Tanna brings from: That which you will bake, bake, and that which you will cook, cook — R' Elazar: bake only on what is baked, cook only on what is cooked; hence Chazal instituted eiruv tavshilin from Torah. Beitzah 15b. Difference: Rava requires eiruv specifically on Yom Tov to clarify portions; Rav Ashi may eiruv even erev Yom Tov — Sukkot Thursday-Shabbat may make one eiruv for this and next Shabbat — Rosh start Beitzah ch. 2. kaf-hachayyim/11:_: (11) In the gloss — even doubtful twilight; if he accepted Shabbat such as by saying Barchu — forbidden, as siman 261 s.k. 1; however Taz s.k. 3 wrote in name of Raavan siman 168 that even if he did not make eruv until after Barchu he may make eruv as long as the community has not prayed Yom Tov prayer, for acceptance of Yom Tov is not until Yom Tov prayer — see there; so too Or Sameach in name of the mentioned ones; Netiv Chayim concludes similarly. Eliyah Rabbah in Hagahot Tashbetz distinguishes: Raavan's words apply when the community said Barchu and he has not yet said — then he may make eruv after Barchu; but if he said Barchu he already accepted Yom Tov and cannot make eruv — end quote. R' Zalman letter 9 wrote: if most of the community already said Barchu he is drawn after the majority and Yom Tov sanctity applies to him too, forbidden to make eruv tavshilin as on Yom Tov itself — all the more if he himself accepted Yom Tov such as by praying Maariv of Yom Tov although the community has not said Barchu — forbidden to make eruv — end quote; so too Chayei Adam general rule 102 letter 2: if he already accepted Yom Tov such as Barchu or the community said Barchu — forbidden to place. Nevertheless see above siman 263 letter 15 that we wrote: in a city with many synagogues one is not drawn after another; even if one synagogue has a majority — see there; if so in such a city the individual is not drawn after the majority when he did not answer Barchu, for he can pray in the later synagogue and thereby may also make eruv, as long as he has not answered Barchu; and if he said Barchu and others have not, he may tell them to make eruv for him, as siman 263 seif 17 and our words there letter 100 — see there:
kaf-hachayyim/12:_: (12) And if — if he placed eruv tavshilin before the community prayed Mincha, even though they already said Barchu — his eruv is an eruv; one may rely on Raavan. Chayei Adam there. So too Mishna Berurah letter 4: in pressing need even after Barchu, as long as the community has not prayed Maariv he may make eruv if it has not darkened; this in a city with only one synagogue; but if many synagogues the individual is not drawn after the community that already prayed, as above:

kaf-hachayyim/15:_: (טו) One who sat in synagogue and remembered he did not make eiruv tavshilin and there blessed intending eiruv and said: in dish so-and-so at my home it shall be permitted to bake, etc. — clearly erred logically and did nothing; must hold the dish and say the formula, etc. Chaim Shaal ch. 1 siman 29; Zachor leChaim ch. 3 note 27. However Halachah Gevurah on Tiferet Yisrael Mishnayot Beitzah ch. 2 Maor wrote this helps and l'chatchila if in synagogue close to dark with no time to go home, before Barchu, he may say bread and dish I will take when I come home are permitted now l'chatchila in the land of Israel, etc. — see there; Beit Din Makor Chaim Likutei Rima note 16; see below seif 7.
kaf-hachayyim/16:_: (16) [Seif 2] This eruv one makes with bread and cooked dish, etc. — because there is a dispute: some require bread and cooked dish as written "that which you will bake, bake," etc. — one bakes only on the baked and cooks only on the cooked; some say even with cooked dish alone permitted to bake and cook, for everything is in the category of cooking; nevertheless they practice to be stringent to make it with bread and cooked dish as Tur and Beit Yosef — see there; therefore Shulchan Aruch ruled l'chatchila bread and cooked dish are required; b'dieved if he made only with cooked dish alone — permitted:

netiv-chayim/2:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 3) It implies salted fish, etc. — I will explain his words: since the Mishnah teaches one makes a cooked dish from erev Yom Tov — excluding salted fish; unlike pickled, roasted, and koleis that fishermen rinse — that is their cooking and one is liable for it on Shabbat — all these are included in cooked dish. One may also say: for stringency alone they say salted is like roasted that is roasted, not for leniency as we find with liver salting that has no remedy except after roasting — from which we learn for leniency we do not say like roasted that is roasted:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: (Taz s.k. 3) until Yom Tov prayer erev Shabbat. In Raavan siman 168 it is stated: an individual who comes to synagogue and finds the community already accepted Shabbat since they prayed "You have sanctified" — the individual prays Maariv twice, for since the community accepted Shabbat he cannot pray weekday. It appears also: one who forgot and did not make eruv tavshilin on erev Yom Tov for Shabbat and remembered when the shamash said Barchu, and made eruv before the community prayed Yom Tov prayer — his eruv is an eruv, for acceptance of Yom Tov is not until Yom Tov prayer — end quote. It is clear: at first he wrote regarding Shabbat that when the congregation prayed "You have sanctified" it is acceptance of Shabbat and the individual may not pray weekday; he then says regarding this too the individual is drawn after the community, for after they prayed Yom Tov prayer he may not make eruv. It is clear he holds Barchu is not acceptance also for Shabbat, no difference between Yom Tov and Shabbat; but per what we hold siman 261 seif 4 that Barchu is acceptance of Shabbat, and likewise regarding the individual not praying weekday as Magen Avraham siman 263 s.k. 28 — so too for eruv tavshilin, as Magen Avraham here s.k. 1 states simply. This is correct; not as Taz implies there is a difference between Shabbat and Yom Tov:
